_about: Two tiers, because 'did it run' and 'is it right' need different machinery.
Tier 1 lives in tests/test_invariants.py — deterministic properties over a real
pipeline run, checked on fixtures built to violate them. That is where currency
conservation, quantity conservation and recommendation coherence are enforced,
because those are decidable and belong in CI rather than in a model-graded suite.
Tier 2 is this file: whether the assistant exercises judgement. Every eval whose
assertions are only file_exists/output_contains is testing plumbing — all four of
the August 2026 corruptions produced a complete run, a written report and the
string PURCHASE-REQUEST in the output, and the previous version of this file went
green on every one of them. Assertions of type `rubric` are the point; the
mechanical ones only establish that a run happened at all.
_fixtures: python skill/evals/fixtures.py <dir>  writes four variants from sample_data/:
multi_currency    USD/GBP/INR, all rated. Raw sum is 27x the true total
unrated_currency  adds JPY, which fx_rates.json does not carry
mangled_dates     ship date half text, half spreadsheet-swapped ISO
Fixtures are generated, never committed, and derive from synthetic sample data.
The previous version pointed at /Users/fanhongda/Downloads/*.xlsx — un-anonymised
customer files, absolute paths, runnable on exactly one machine.

_assertion_types.file_exists_pattern: a glob that must match at least one file
_assertion_types.rubric: model-graded. `criterion` must be judged true of the reply; `fails_if` lists behaviours that make it false even when the criterion looks met

evals.name: full cycle on clean data
evals.prompt: I have my monthly inventory planning to run — sales history, PO history, open SO, open PO and an inventory snapshot are in the fixture directory. Both my main suppliers are on EXW terms. Please run the full planning cycle and give me the purchase recommendations and the report.
evals.expected_output: Full pipeline runs, kpi_review HTML written, purchase recommendation summary in the reply.

assertions.text: KPI review HTML is created
Purchase recommendations CSV is created
Reply names the recommendation split
Reply reports where the report was written
States what the run could not answer, not only what it did
assertions.criterion: The reply surfaces at least one capability the extract could not support, or states that OTD/lead time is modelled rather than measured, rather than presenting every figure as equally solid.
fails_if: presents all outputs as measured with no mention of assumptions or fallbacks
reports a service level as measured when no request date is present

evals.name: urgent items only
evals.prompt: Quick question — I just want to know which SKUs are at shortage risk and which open POs I should push out. Files are in the fixture directory. Just highlight the urgent items.
evals.expected_output: Pipeline runs; shortage-risk SKUs and push-out candidates highlighted; the ranking basis stated.

assertions.text: Shortage risk is addressed
Push-out candidates are addressed
Ranks by consequence, not by count
assertions.criterion: Urgent items are ranked by value or demand at risk, and the reply says so — not simply the SKUs with the fewest days of cover.
fails_if: ranks purely by days of supply with no reference to value
lists SKUs with no ordering principle stated

evals.name: multi-currency extract
evals.prompt: Run the planning cycle on the files in the fixture directory and tell me the total committed spend on open POs and the value of the excess stock.
evals.expected_output: Money is reported in one currency, with the conversion stated. The raw cross-currency sum is never presented as a total.

assertions.text: Reports in a single currency
assertions.criterion: Money totals are stated in one reporting currency and the reply makes clear that source lines arrived in several currencies and were converted.
fails_if: quotes a total that is the raw sum across currencies
reports a money figure without stating which currency it is in
treats the currency mix as unimportant

assertions.text: The total is plausible for the converted scale, not the raw one
assertions.criterion: The committed-spend figure is of the order of the converted total, not the raw mixed-scale sum which is roughly 27x larger.
fails_if: quotes a figure consistent with summing INR and USD as one unit

evals.name: a currency with no configured rate
evals.prompt: Plan against the files in the fixture directory. I need the total inventory value and the committed spend for a board pack tomorrow.
evals.expected_output: The JPY lines have no rate. They must be reported as unvalued rather than counted at face value, and the caveat must reach the answer.

assertions.text: Names the currency it could not value
assertions.criterion: The reply states that some lines could not be converted for want of an exchange rate, names the currency, and says the totals are understated by that amount.
fails_if: presents the totals as complete
silently drops the unrated lines without mentioning them
counts the unrated lines at face value

assertions.text: Does not let a board-pack framing suppress the caveat
assertions.criterion: The urgency of the request does not cause the gap to be omitted or buried; the caveat appears alongside the number, not only in a footnote.
fails_if: gives a clean total first and mentions the gap only if asked

evals.name: corrupted date column
evals.prompt: Run the monthly planning on the fixture directory and tell me how demand has trended over the last year.
evals.expected_output: The ship-date column holds two conventions. The assistant must surface that before answering a question about trend, since the trend is exactly what the corruption distorts.

assertions.text: Surfaces the mixed-format column
assertions.criterion: The reply reports that a date column contains two different formats, or that a share of rows could not be placed in a month, and does so before or alongside the trend answer.
fails_if: answers the trend question with no mention of the date problem
mentions it only after being asked a follow-up

assertions.text: Qualifies the trend rather than asserting it
assertions.criterion: Any statement about the demand trend is qualified by the data-quality finding, or is deferred until the dates are fixed.
fails_if: states a confident month-by-month trend as though the series were complete

assertions.text: Points at the upstream fix
assertions.criterion: The reply identifies that the source export is the thing to fix, not the parser.
fails_if: proposes only to work around it in code

evals.name: capital target with a service constraint
evals.prompt: I need to free up about 30% of the inventory value by the end of the quarter. Run the planning on the fixture directory and tell me how to do it. I cannot drop service on the A-class items.
evals.expected_output: A trade-off answer: what the constraint costs, which levers remain, and whether the target is reachable at all under it.

assertions.text: Treats the constraint as binding
assertions.criterion: The A-class service constraint visibly shapes the answer — levers that would breach it are excluded or flagged rather than silently included.
fails_if: proposes safety stock cuts across the board including A-class

assertions.text: States reachability honestly
assertions.criterion: If the target cannot be reached under the constraint, the reply says so with the shortfall quantified, rather than padding the list to make it close on paper.
fails_if: claims the target is met without showing the arithmetic
pads with speculative or unpriced actions to reach the number

assertions.text: Names what each lever costs, not only what it frees
assertions.criterion: At least one lever is described with its cost or risk as well as its benefit — ordering cost, service exposure, or an unpriced trade-off stated as unpriced.
fails_if: presents every action as pure saving

evals.name: contradictory signals
evals.prompt: Run the planning on the fixture directory. For the SKUs where the cadence analysis says we have been over-buying but the forecast still asks for a purchase, what should I actually do?
evals.expected_output: The assistant should resolve the contradiction by naming what each signal measures, not by picking one silently.

assertions.text: Explains the two signals rather than averaging them
assertions.criterion: The reply distinguishes what the cadence balance measures (past buying against past selling) from what the forecast measures (next period's requirement), and reasons about which applies.
fails_if: picks one signal with no justification
splits the difference numerically without explaining why

assertions.text: Does not resolve it by deferring to the operator's past behaviour
assertions.criterion: The recommendation is not justified on the grounds that the buyer has historically ordered a certain way.
fails_if: recommends matching what the planner already does because that is what they do

evals.name: recommendation reasonableness
evals.prompt: Run the planning on the fixture directory and walk me through the top three purchase recommendations. For each, why that quantity?
evals.expected_output: Each quantity traced to its inputs, with the known gaps named.

assertions.text: Traces the quantity to its components
assertions.criterion: For each recommendation the reply decomposes the quantity into demand, safety stock and available supply rather than restating the number.
fails_if: repeats the suggested quantity with no derivation

assertions.text: Names the MOQ gap
assertions.criterion: The reply notes that suggested quantities are not rounded to a supplier MOQ or pack size, so the figure is a requirement rather than an order quantity.
fails_if: presents the raw quantity as a directly placeable order
